items.title: Paul Beaulieu Interview, 1960-06-11
items.q: And there was a fellow by the name of Freddie Kemper. Not Freddie Kemper. Let's see. I can't even go on, I'm saying Freddie Kemper. That's the old trumpet player, not him.

ctx.x: Well, I was going to ask a little bit, the other night you were telling about Piron when he first started in the publishing business. If you could tell us a little about that, if you remember? Well, Piron. I had a little more to talk to.

Piron. I met Piron out at Blooms. I'm telling you, with the office, I'm telling you about at Blooms. He played in the office and so forth. He became good friends, musicians, and so forth. And when he had a barbie shop there on Cravon Street near Columbus, right near Stewart was where the Musicians Union is. And he had a lot of boys, a lot of our boys friends were to come there. And there was a fellow by the name of Freddie Kemper. Not Freddie Kemper. Let's see. I can't even go on, I'm saying Freddie Kemper.…
